citations.title: OpenAI | Koodisi Documentation
excerpts: # OpenAI Activities
Use the OpenAI group to work with the models available to your OpenAI account. The activities call the OpenAI REST API and return its response to the workflow.
## Available activities ​
|Activity |Purpose |
|[**List Models**](https://docs.koodisi.com/working-with-activities/list-of-available-activities/openai/listmodels/) |Returns the models available to the account |
|[**Retrieve Model**](https://docs.koodisi.com/working-with-activities/list-of-available-activities/openai/retrievemodel/) |Returns details of a single model |
|[**Delete Model**](https://docs.koodisi.com/working-with-activities/list-of-available-activities/openai/deletemodel/) |Deletes a fine-tuned model |
## Configure an OpenAI call ​
1. Add the activity to the workflow.
2. Supply the OpenAI API key as an `Authorization` header on the **Headers** tab.
3. For **Retrieve Model** and **Delete Model** , enter the **Model Name** .
4. Map the request on the **Input** tab and the response on the **Output** tab.

citations.title: AI | Koodisi Documentation
excerpts: ## Build an AI workflow ​
1. Configure the required provider and credentials as resources or managed secrets.
2. Add **LLM Provider** for direct model calls, or **AI Agent** for tool-using, multi-step behavior.
3. Add memory only when the workflow needs context across interactions.
4. Add **Embedding Model** and **Vector DB** for retrieval-augmented generation or semantic search.
5. Add **MCP** only for approved servers and tools.
6. Map model output through validation and business rules before it reaches a write operation.
## Safety and governance ​
* Do not place secrets, regulated data, or unnecessary personal information in prompts.
* Treat model output as untrusted input and validate it before executing commands or changing records.
* Restrict MCP and other tools to the minimum required permissions.
* Require human confirmation for consequential or irreversible actions.
* Set token, timeout, and iteration limits to control cost and prevent loops.
* Record provider, model, prompt version, tool calls, and outcome where audit policy permits.

This supports OpenAI as an available provider, not a claim that it is the default backend for all Koodisi AI features.

citations.title: V 1.2.7 | Koodisi Documentation
excerpts: ## Agent Studio (Beta) ​
Agent Studio is a new Studio capability for building your own AI agents using the integrations you have already built and governed in Koodisi.
* **Your activities as tools.** Agents call the activities you have already built, each with its own OAuth connection, using the same connections and permissions.
* **Agents that work together.** Agents can hand work to other agents (A2A). The canvas shows how they are connected.
* **Connect external tools.** Agents connect to MCP servers, with OAuth sign-in built into the Agent Builder.
## Koodisi AI: build, deploy and test from the chat ​
Koodisi AI brings workflow building, deployment and testing into one place, taking a workflow from first draft to tested deployment without leaving the chat.

* **Better workflow building, with a live preview.** Koodisi AI builds workflows more reliably, including subflows, mappings and tables. The canvas preview updates as each change lands, so you review the result while Koodisi AI works.
* **Revert changes.** Undo the changes Koodisi AI made and return the workflow to its earlier state.
* **Create alerts from the chat.** Describe what you want to monitor and Koodisi AI sets up the alert. Review a confirmation card before the alert is saved.

* **Publish, deploy and test.** Koodisi AI publishes and deploys using the same steps as the Deploy dialog, with a changelog that names every step and field that changed. Test runs resume after a deploy, and failures include buttons that take you to the problem.

leadership_change_12mo.notes: The official team page lists the small leadership roster; no C-level or VP-level join or departure in the 12-month window is shown or announced in the checked sources.
